practiceReport.name: Kenneth Walker III
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Every-down starter workload (74% snaps) — 82% active conversion baseline when logging Limited Friday reps.
factors: Officially ruled Out on weekly game status report
practiceReport.beatComment: Though Walker was able to log a limited practice Tuesday, he was listed as a non-participant Wednesday and will wind up missing a third straight contest while he continues to nurse a sore groin. With Walker sidelined, rookie Emmett Johnson is set for another turn as the Chiefs' lead back, with Jaydn Ott serving as his top backup and Nate Carter a possible practice-squad elevation. Given that the Chiefs on are on a short week, Walker -- who last saw game action Nov. 8 -- will have added time to heal before the team's next contest Dec. 3 against the Rams.

practiceReport.name: Patrick Mahomes
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Veteran starter profile (10th NFL season, 97% snap share) — elevated Questionable active conversion (84%) & Wednesday maintenance tolerance.
practiceReport.beatComment: Mahomes was clicking early against the Cardinals' defense, capping off the opening possession of the game with an eight-yard touchdown toss to Travis Kelce. The prolific signal-caller went on to add a 22-yard scoring pass to Kelce shortly before the end of the first half, and he capped off his day with an 18-yarder to Xavier Worthy on which the speedy receiver raced up the right sideline and into the end zone. Mahomes now has consecutive 300-yard efforts and has accomplished the feat in three of the past four games overall, affording him plenty of momentum heading into a Week 12 showdown with Josh Allen and the Bills on Thanksgiving night.

practiceReport.name: Trey Smith
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Every-down starter workload (91% snaps) — 82% active conversion baseline when logging Limited Friday reps.
practiceReport.beatComment: Smith has logged two consecutive full practices, and while Smith is in the league's concussion protocol, head coach Andy Reid said Tuesday that he anticipates that Smith will be available for Thursday's game against the Bills, per Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star. If he's cleared to play Thanksgiving Day, Smith would likely reclaim his starting job at right guard while Mike Caliendo reverts to a depth role.

practiceReport.name: Rashee Rice
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Perimeter speed/cut position (WR) — requires full deceleration/burst clearance on lower-body tags (76% Questionable baseline).
practiceReport.beatComment: Rice tied for the team lead in receptions and finished as the runner-up in targets to Travis Kelce. The veteran receiver averaged a modest 8.8 yards per catch, his third game in the last four with under 10.0 yards per reception. Rice has at least five catches in four consecutive contests heading into Thursday's Week 12 Thanksgiving showdown against the Bills in Buffalo.

practiceReport.name: Noah Gray
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Standard NFL positional availability baseline (78% Questionable conversion).
practiceReport.beatComment: Though Gray was listed as a full participant on both Tuesday and Wednesday's injury reports, the Chiefs' TE2 will nonetheless carry a 'questionable" designation ahead of Week 12 action. With a 10/211/1 receiving line through 10 contests thus far, Gray is only an option in the deepest of fantasy formats, at least as long as Travis Kelce is available.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Brashard Smith
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Smith sustained a hamstring injury in Thursday's practice session and has promptly been transitioned to IR as he manages the issue. Running back Jaydn Ott has been signed to the active roster to be the No. 3 option behind Kenneth Walker and Emmett Johnson while Smith recovers.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Josh Simmons
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Though he had been on the Chiefs' 53-man roster all season, Simmons had yet to make his 2026 debut while working his way back from a bulging and herniated disc in his lower back. Simmons appeared to be making strides in his recovery after he returned to practice last week as a limited participant, but he downgraded to no participation Wednesday after head trainer Rick Burkholder said that the second-year left tackle "plateaued in the rehab process," per Nate Taylor of ESPN.com. As a result, the Chiefs have opted to deactivate Simmons, who won't be eligible to play until Week 11 versus the Cardinals. Undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson should continue to start at left tackle in Simmons' absence.

irAndReserveTracker.name: L'Jarius Sneed
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Sneed was initially given the questionable tag for Sunday's game against the Broncos. He's been able to play through a lingering knee issue, but his placement on IR indicates that the injury has gotten to the point that an extended absence is warranted for the seventh-year defensive back. Sneed will be required to miss at least four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 12 against the Bills on Thursday, Nov. 26. Jaden Hicks, Jadon Canady, Kristian Fulton and Christian Roland-Wallace are all candidates to see more work in the secondary due to the absences of both Sneed and Mansoor Delane (shoulder) for Sunday's AFC West tilt.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Jared Wiley
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Wiley was carted to the locker room in the first quarter of the Chiefs' Week 10 win over the Falcons with an ankle injury. The tight end will now be on IR as he nurses his fractured ankle until at least the latter part of the regular season. Travis Kelce, Noah Gray and Jake Briningstool are now the only tight ends on the Chiefs' active roster.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Ben VanSumeren
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: VanSumeren didn't practice Tuesday due to a sprained knee that will now keep him out for at least the next four weeks, according to Matt McMullen of the Chiefs' official site. In six regular-season games in 2026, the fourth-year pro played a majority of his reps on special teams, with just six of 104 total snaps coming on offense.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Tyquan Thornton
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: The transaction frees up a spot on the 53-man roster for linebacker Cam Jones, who was signed off the practice squad. After dislocating his left ankle in the Chiefs' Oct. 4 win over the Raiders and requiring surgery, Thornton is facing an estimated recovery timeline of 3-to-4 months, which means that he'll likely be sidelined until at least Week 17 or 18 in a best-case scenario. While Thornton is out, the Chiefs are expected to lean on Jalen Royals and Cyrus Allen to handle more reps in three-receiver sets alongside starters Rashee Rice (hamstring) and Xavier Worthy.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Ethan Downs
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Downs' season is over after he tore his ACL during Tuesday's practice session. The 23-year-old will now shift his focus to getting healthy, and he will look to make his NFL debut during the 2027 campaign.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Jeff Caldwell
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Caldwell hyperextended his left knee during Wednesday's practice and was promptly waived with an injury designation. The wide receiver will now spend the entirety of the 2026 regular season on injured reserve unless he is waived with an injury settlement.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Jimmy Holiday
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Holiday is dealing with an undisclosed injury, and he did not play during the preseason. The wide receiver will now be forced to miss the entire 2026 campaign while on IR, unless he is able to reach an injury settlement with Kansas City.

irAndReserveTracker.name: John Michael Gyllenborg
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Placed on Injured Reserve (Knee) on Jul 28, 2026; ineligible to return in 2026 under NFL CBA rules.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Matt Waletzko
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Waletzko did not get claimed after the Chiefs waived him with an undisclosed injury Thursday, and he's now in line to spend the entire 2026 on IR. He last suited up for a regular-season contest back in 2024 with the Cowboys.
